mrob · Nov 28, 2026

IMO, any system that was exploited by this was already insecure. It's not exploiting bugs in the inference engine or attempting any kind of sandbox escape. Here the exploit was in the chat template, but it's possible to encode the same thing directly in the weights. Unless the model is truly Open Source (not just open weight), there's no way to know what malicious instructions might be encoded in the weights. The only defense is to sandbox the agent sufficiently strongly that it can't do harm no matter what tokens it generates. In such a sandbox, it doesn't matter that the payload was stored directly in the GGUF file, because it won't be able to do anything with it anyway.
